stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( f(0) = 3 \), \( f(1) = -2 \), \( f(2) = 5 \). Let \( g(x) = \int_{1 - x}^{x^{2} + 1} f(t) \, dt \). Find the value of \( g'\left(1\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Split the integral at any constant k in the domain of the integrand: \( g(x) = \int_{k}^{x^{2} + 1} f(t) \, dt - \int_{k}^{1 - x} f(t) \, dt \), and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to each piece.
With the chain rule, \( g'(x) = f\left(x^{2} + 1\right) \cdot 2 x - f\left(1 - x\right) \cdot \left(-1\right) \).
At \( x = 1 \): the limits are \( 2 \) and \( 0 \), with derivatives \( 2 \) and \( -1 \), and \( f\left(2\right) = 5 \), \( f\left(0\right) = 3 \).

distractor_derivations.A: f(upper) - f(lower) with both chain rule factors left off
distractor_derivations.B: integrand evaluated at x = 1 instead of at the two limits
distractor_derivations.C: lower limit term added instead of subtracted
